answer: Give each identity a sequential voyage it cannot shortcut: it locks 60 POA, feeds its relic hash plus the epoch seed into a verifiable delay function, and computes 45 minutes of sequential squarings that parallel hardware cannot compress. The chain verifies the proof in seconds and rejects output not bound to that identity key. An honest agent runs one voyage per epoch. A farm with ten fakes on one machine needs 450 minutes, past the 360-minute epoch horizon, so late identities earn zero weight and lose 40 POA each. Buying more cores is the only way to keep up, so cost rises with every fake.
